title: Arrive at the destination
summary: A prize for arriving, and why a prize on its own teaches nothing.

steps.title: A prize for arriving
steps.body:
Progress pays a little all the way. Arriving should pay the most, because getting there is the whole point of the trip.

Give 10 points when `car.arrived` is true. On empty streets the SUV arrives once its middle is inside the destination zone and it is under the speed limit. The test driver arrives, so its score should pass 10.

check.message: The test drive should score more than 10 points.

hints: car.arrived is true on the tick the SUV arrives.
Replace the comment with reward +10 when car.arrived.

steps.title: Rewards that come too late
steps.body:
Press Check. It trains 40 SUVs for 15 generations and reports the most of the route a generation covered.

This script only pays for arriving. Untrained brains almost never arrive, so they all score 0, and evolution cannot tell a brain that drove 200 m from one that never moved. A reward that almost never happens is called a sparse reward.

Pay for progress as well, so every meter counts.

check.message: Training should cover more than 30% of the route.

hints: route.gain is the new ground covered this tick.
Add reward +0.02 * route.gain above the prize.

steps.title: Read the score
steps.body:
Fitness adds up every reward of a trip. With 0.02 points a meter, a 220 m trip pays about 4.4 for the drive and 10 for arriving, so arriving is worth more than all the driving before it.

That is on purpose: a brain that drives well but never stops in the zone should lose to one that does. Make the progress reward a little bigger, 0.03 a meter, and see the test drive score rise.

check.message: The test drive should score more than 16 points.

hints: Change the number in front of route.gain.
